control_interpretation_rules: Each case starts a separately authorized fresh bounded process with the same model/fixture seeds and pinned deterministic runtime profile; no automatic continuation after failure.

Both SPMM controls first execute native support, eval encoder and full-node xlin. Require an observed CONTROL_NATIVE_COMMON_SUPPORT marker and entry to native.spmm_add before attributing a subsequent first error to that sparse-call boundary.
A successful zero-nnz control shows that geometry is not sufficient to fail in that fresh control context; it does not eliminate a history-dependent mechanism in exact.
An empty_spmm failure at its synchronized sparse boundary would establish a separate zero-row sparse reproducer. It would not by itself explain the nonempty addmm failure in exact.
If SPMM controls complete but depth0 fails, use that control first-error trace to locate the extra forward operations; do not name a dense head from completion/failure status alone.

All four controls completing would leave exact recursion/history or unrecorded state differences unresolved. The four controls do not include a standalone [16,64] addmm/xlin reproducer or a matched recursive-history intervention.
No control is a full native qualification: no complete arm coverage, training/backward, optimizer/restore/RNG parity or output oracle is provided by diagnostic completion.

limitations: Only FIRST_ERROR, traceback, terminal metadata and the last16 operator events were copied locally; the full OPERATORS.jsonl and earlier native-call stage markers were not reviewed.

Metadata establishes compatible nonempty dense shapes, dtype and device; it does not establish input values, finiteness, strides/storage alignment, autograd grad-enabled state, kernel choice, workspace validity or memory/context integrity.

Successful fences support current-call localization and weigh against simple delayed reporting from the displayed preceding operations. They do not exclude latent earlier corruption or low-level suppressed errors.

TorchDispatchMode, synchronization and fsync instrumentation pass original overload arguments unchanged but perturb timing/dispatch context. The earlier uninstrumented qualification error at xlin/F.linear corroborates the site, without identifying the underlying cause.

No remote runtime/kernel/model/data/checkpoint investigation or rerun was performed. Runtime and binary identity rests on matching authenticated receipts and file-custody guards; no runtime binary was independently read.
